restatement: Give the headless template-resolver core a command line (template-resolver) with render, validate, analyze, spec and serve subcommands, built only on node built-ins over the existing core and HTTP API. It reads a template and data from files or stdin (only one from stdin), prints only the result on stdout, prints located diagnostics on stderr, and uses the exit codes design.md documents: 0 ok, 1 template error, 2 usage or I/O error. Render limits and strictness are passed through as flags, serve starts the API and shuts down cleanly, and main(argv, io) is exported so it can be tested without spawning a process.
brief_mismatch: m2 says stdout carries nothing but the result, but the frozen cl-serve test reads the listening address from stdout. The diff prints 'listening on http://host:port' there. That is reasonable if the address counts as serve's result, but the brief should say so.
verification_plan: c1: render with a template file and a data file prints exactly result.output with no added newline and exits 0. Template or data from '-' reads stdin. No --data means empty data.
c1: a template error (missing variable in strict mode, or a syntax error) leaves stdout empty, writes file:line:col: error code: message to stderr with the real file name and line, and exits 1.
c1: --json prints the full RenderResult on success and on failure, and the exit code stays 0 or 1.
c2: validate prints {ok, diagnostics} JSON and exits 1 when not ok. analyze prints JSON including required and blocks. spec prints the spec JSON with every top-level key.

c3: no args, an unknown subcommand, an unknown option, a missing template or data file, invalid or non-object data JSON, both inputs on stdin and a non-numeric limit each exit 2 with stderr text and empty stdout. --help prints usage on stdout and exits 0.
c4: each of --strict, --no-strict, --max-iterations, --max-output-chars and --max-depth changes the render options (check the limit-* diagnostic codes, and that a run within a limit passes).
c5: serve listens on the given host and port, answers POST /v1/render, and closes the server and its connections when the signal aborts.
m1: package.json has no new runtime dependency. Imports are fs, util, core and api only.
m2: nothing other than the result goes to stdout (no logs or debug output).
m3: the serve test closes its server and leaves no open handle.
Scope: only files under cli/ change. The bin entry resolves to the built cli/index.js and the compiled binary behaves the same as main().

findings.title: analyze on an unparseable template prints a stderr diagnostic instead of JSON

serves.scenario: design.md says analyze prints JSON. When the template has a syntax error, analyze writes '<file>:1:1: error syntax-error: ...' to stderr, leaves stdout empty and exits 1. A caller that pipes analyze into a JSON parser gets no JSON. The criterion does not specify the error case, so this is noted rather than asked to be fixed.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: printf '{{IF a}}x' | template-resolver analyze -  -> stderr '<stdin>:1:1: error syntax-error: Unclosed {{IF}} block...', stdout empty, exit 1
